title: Immutable evaluation economics with human judgment correction
prompt:
# Evaluation ledger: candidate contract, stage 0

Implement `from evalledger import Ledger` using only Python's standard library.
The package already has `store.py`, `ledger.py`, and `economics.py`; repair the
multi-file package. `Ledger(path)` is durable across close/reopen (there is no
close method), with each successful mutation persisted before returning. There is
one writer at a time, no concurrent object instances, and no process kill inside a
single method. Failed mutations must leave memory and disk unchanged. Public
tests are immutable. You may add checks under `candidate_tests/`.

All identifiers are nonempty strings of length <=128. All integer inputs below
must be actual Python ints, never bools. Lists contain <=1000 members and ledgers
contain <=10000 records; huge integers and arbitrary object inputs are out of scope.
For invalid contract inputs raise ValueError, including missing tenant/run/task.
Public methods return detached values: caller mutation cannot change the ledger.
Keys and identities must remain separate across tenants and runs, including IDs
containing separators such as `:`. Preserve the named module imports.

* `register_run(tenant, run_id, revision, task_ids, primary_metric) -> bool` freezes
  the definition revision, ordered distinct nonempty task IDs (>=1), and explicitly
  pinned primary metric revision. Returns True on creation, False on exact replay.
  Reusing the tenant/run with any changed field raises ValueError.
* `record_operation(tenant, run_id, operation) -> bool`: operation has exactly
  `id, task_id, kind, invoked, replay, status, cost_microusd`. kind is workflow or
  judge; status is succeeded or failed; invoked/replay are bools; cost_microusd is
  None or an int in 0..1_000_000_000. Identity is operation id within that tenant/run.
  Exact replay returns False; changed content raises ValueError; new returns True.
  Distinct retries have distinct IDs and must all be charged if invoked, even when
  failed. Replay operations and non-invoked operations are excluded from billable
  cost and cost coverage, regardless of their cost field. Task must be registered.
* `complete_task(tenant, run_id, task_id) -> bool` adds a registered task to the
  completed set: True once, then False. Completion alone is not quality acceptance.
* `record_review(tenant, run_id, review) -> bool`: review has exactly
  `id, task_id, metric_revision, status, sequence, passed`. status is completed or
  pending. sequence is int 0..1_000_000. completed requires bool passed; pending
  requires passed=None. Identity/replay/conflict semantics match operations.
  A task's quality uses only completed reviews of the pinned metric, choosing max
  `(sequence, id)` lexicographically; later pending reviews do not hide completed
  ones. Quality does not depend on operational completion.
* `snapshot(tenant, run_id) -> dict` returns the frozen run plus evidence as
  `revision, task_ids, primary_metric, operations, completed, reviews`, where
  operations/reviews are insertion-order lists of original records and completed
  is a sorted task-id list. It must be detached.
* `summary(tenant, run_id) -> dict` returns exactly these values:
  `planned`, `completed`, `evaluated`, `accepted`, `billable_operations`,
  `priced_operations` (integer counts); `review_coverage=evaluated/planned`,
  `planned_success=accepted/planned`, `pass_rate=accepted/evaluated` (None if none);
  `cost_coverage=priced/billable` (1.0 if no billable operations);
  `known_cost_usd` (sum of known billable amounts), `total_cost_usd` (None if any
  billable amount unknown), `cost_per_accepted_usd` (None unless total is known and
  accepted>0). Dollar amounts are strings with exactly six decimal places,
  rounding only the final division with decimal ROUND_HALF_UP; 1_000_000 microUSD
  = 1 USD. Do not round individual operations, drop failed attempts, double charge
  retries, substitute completed for accepted, or turn missing costs into zero.

Run provided tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`; final hidden
tests evaluate the full contract. Finish with a concise summary and verification.
followup:
Authoritative stage 1 change: reviewers can retract an incorrect judgment without
rewriting history. Keep every stage-0 behavior and API working. Add
`retract_review(tenant, run_id, review_id, retraction_id, reason) -> bool`.
Both IDs use the existing identifier rules; reason is a nonempty string <=500
characters. The target must already exist in this run, including pending or
non-primary reviews. Retraction identity is retraction_id within tenant/run:
an exact replay returns False, changed target or reason raises ValueError, new
returns True. Multiple different retraction IDs for the same review are allowed
and each new receipt returns True. Persist each receipt atomically. Reviews remain
unchanged and present in snapshot.reviews; add snapshot.retractions, an insertion
order list of dicts with `id, review_id, reason`. Summary must exclude all retracted
reviews before choosing the latest completed primary judgment, falling back to
the previous eligible one. If none remains the task is unevaluated. Costs,
operational completion, and run pins never change because of a retraction. A
review recorded later cannot reuse an existing review ID with altered content,
even if retracted. Reopen must preserve retractions. Test the correction and
regression behavior; original public tests remain immutable.

Preserve all stage-0 data already present under carryover/LR1/ while implementing this follow-up. It was created using your stage-0 public APIs. You may inspect it through those APIs; do not reset or discard existing data. The final checks will reopen that same store with your updated implementation.

title: Versioned tenant retrieval with independently changing compliance policy
prompt:
# Versioned tenant retrieval: candidate contract, stage 0

Implement `from retrieval import DocumentIndex` in the existing multi-file Python
stdlib package (`store.py`, `index.py`, `query.py`). `DocumentIndex(path)` persists
all successful changes before returning and reopens identical state. Single writer,
no concurrent instances or mid-method process kill. Failed mutations change
neither memory nor disk. Public tests remain unchanged; candidate_tests/ is allowed.
All identifiers/tags are nonempty strings <=128 characters; body is any string
<=10000 characters. Actual integer versions are 0..1_000_000 (bool is invalid).
Each batch <=1000 documents and dataset <=10000 documents; huge values out of scope.
Invalid inputs, missing required fields or conflicting identities raise ValueError.

* `apply_batch(tenant, batch_id, events) -> bool`: events is a list of dicts with
  exactly `id, version, body, tags, deleted`. tags is a list of distinct valid tag
  strings; its input order IS part of the immutable event payload. deleted is bool.
  Duplicate document IDs within one batch are invalid. Empty batches are allowed.
  Tenant/batch ID scopes an ordered immutable receipt: new valid returns True,
  byte-equivalent Python data replay False, changed event/order raises ValueError.
  Tenant/document identity is separate. Higher version replaces prior content;
  lower version is ignored. Equal version with identical event is ignored; equal
  version with changed content raises ValueError. Tombstones (`deleted=True`)
  retain their version and block stale resurrection. A higher nondeleted version
  may restore a document. Validate/process the entire batch atomically: a late
  conflict cannot leave earlier documents, receipt, or search results changed.
  Store detached copies: caller mutations cannot alter state or receipts.
* `search(tenant, query, limit=10, required_tags=None) -> list[dict]` returns detached
  copies of complete nondeleted event dicts. A missing tenant returns []. query
  must be a string <=10000 characters; limit actual int 0..1000. required_tags is
  None or a list of distinct valid tags. Match ALL query tokens and ALL required
  tags after tenant isolation, before applying limit. Tokens are obtained only
  with `.casefold().split()`; punctuation is not stripped. Repeated query tokens
  count once. Empty/whitespace query matches all eligible documents. Score is the
  sum of frequency in body for each unique query token, empty query score 0.
  Sort by descending score, then ascending document ID. Result ordering must be
  deterministic across restart. Every successful update must be reflected in
  subsequent searches even if the exact query was already used; cache state may
  never leak tenants, filters, limits, tombstones, or old versions.
* `get(tenant, doc_id) -> dict|None` returns a detached latest event including a
  tombstone, or None if absent. Validate identifiers. It ignores search filters.

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`; hidden tests cover the full contract.
Finish with a concise change and verification note.
followup:
Authoritative stage 1 change: compliance exclusions now change independently of
document ingestion. Preserve all stage-0 behavior. Add
`set_policy(tenant, revision, blocked_tags) -> bool`, where tenant is a valid ID,
revision an actual int 0..1_000_000, and blocked_tags a list of distinct valid tags.
Tag order is semantically irrelevant for this policy only; normalize it. A tenant
without policy has no blocked tags. New or higher revision atomically persists
the policy and returns True, lower revision returns False without change, equal
revision with same tag set returns False, equal revision with a different set
raises ValueError. Validate all fields even on stale updates. This API may create
a policy before the tenant has documents. Subsequent search must exclude any
document with ANY blocked tag, including an empty query, before ranking/limit.
Apply the newest policy immediately even for previously cached queries; clearing
the block list at a higher revision restores eligible documents. get() and stored
document versions remain unchanged, and one tenant's policy cannot affect another.
Policies and query results must survive reopen. Document batch changes still
invalidate results under the current policy. Test policy corrections and existing
behavior; do not alter original public tests.

Preserve all stage-0 data already present under carryover/LR2/ while implementing this follow-up. It was created using your stage-0 public APIs. You may inspect it through those APIs; do not reset or discard existing data. The final checks will reopen that same store with your updated implementation.

title: Recoverable chunked export with cancellation after partial work
prompt:
# Durable export queue: candidate contract, stage 0

Implement `from exports import ExportQueue` in the existing Python stdlib package
(`store.py`, `queue.py`, `validation.py`). `ExportQueue(path)` persists all successful
mutations before return; reopening recovers leases, chunks and commit receipts.
Single writer/no concurrent instances; no process kill within a method. The caller
may lose a method's return value and retry, including after reopening. Failed
methods must leave memory and disk unchanged. Public tests are immutable; add your
own tests under candidate_tests/ if useful. All identifiers nonempty strings <=128.
now is an explicit actual int 0..1_000_000_000, ttl actual int 1..1_000_000, bool
invalid. No wall clock, background threads or waits. Dataset <=1000 jobs/tenant;
rows <=1000/job. Invalid contract inputs or missing referenced jobs raise ValueError.

* `submit(tenant, job_id, rows) -> bool`: rows is an ordered list of distinct row-ID
  dicts with exactly `id, value`, valid identifier id and string value <=10000.
  Empty list is allowed. New tenant/job returns True; identical replay False;
  changed ordered rows raise ValueError. Store detached input.
* `claim(tenant, worker, now, ttl) -> dict|None`: choose the lexicographically lowest
  job ID among queued jobs or running jobs whose lease expires <=now. Return
  exactly `job_id, token, cursor`. Mark it running and lease until now+ttl. Tokens
  are nonempty strings, unique across all claims (including restart); worker must
  be a valid identifier. Never reclaim an unexpired lease or completed job. Return
  None for no eligible job. Every claim advances a durable token generator.
* `append(tenant, job_id, token, chunk_id, rows, now) -> bool`: requires this job's
  current live token (running and now<expiry). rows is a nonempty valid row list
  that must exactly match the next contiguous slice of submitted rows; append it
  and advance cursor atomically. Chunk identity is tenant/job/chunk_id. Under a
  live current lease, identical chunk replay returns False even after cursor has
  advanced or a new lease was claimed; changed rows raise ValueError. Check live
  lease BEFORE replay lookup: a stale token cannot write or acknowledge replay.
  Appends may include any positive number of remaining rows. No skipped, reordered,
  duplicated or invented data. Failed append does not consume the chunk ID.
* `commit(tenant, job_id, token, commit_id, now) -> str`: requires current live lease
  and cursor==total rows. Atomically mark completed and persist commit receipt and
  artifact digest. The digest is sha256 of JSON encoding of the complete submitted
  row list using `json.dumps(rows, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'),
  ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')`. A completed job accepts an exact replay of
  its successful token+commit_id, returning the same digest even after expiry;
  any other token/commit_id raises ValueError. No double publication. Validate
  argument shapes even for replay. A commit cannot succeed on a partial export.
* `inspect(tenant, job_id) -> dict` returns exactly detached `state, cursor, total,
  artifact_sha256, lease_expires`, state queued/running/completed; digest None until
  committed, lease_expires None when queued/completed. Expired running jobs remain
  running in inspect until reclaimed. No claim/inspect may silently reset cursor.

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and verify failures/restart/replay.
Finish with a concise change and verification note. Hidden tests check the contract.
followup:
Authoritative stage 1 change: add durable cancellation of uncommitted exports,
including those with staged chunks. Preserve all stage-0 behavior. Add
`cancel(tenant, job_id, request_id) -> bool`, all IDs using existing rules. First
cancellation of a queued/running job changes state to cancelled, clears its lease,
retains cursor/chunk receipts for inspection, leaves artifact_sha256=None, and
returns True. Record the request receipt durably. Cancellation identity is
tenant/request_id (across jobs): exact replay returns False, reusing a request ID
for a different job raises ValueError without changing either job. A fresh request
ID for an already cancelled job is recorded and returns False. Completed jobs
cannot be cancelled: raise ValueError without reserving that request ID. A job's
existing submit receipt remains immutable after cancellation. Cancelled jobs are
never claimable and every append/commit (including old successful chunk replay)
must raise ValueError. inspect returns state='cancelled', retained cursor/total,
artifact_sha256=None and lease_expires=None. One tenant's receipt or cancellation
cannot affect another tenant. No explicit undo/resume API is requested. Test late
cancellation, restart and replay; keep original public tests unchanged.
